To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MIA PaCA-2 and PANT-1 xenografted models are useful for selecting anticancer agents for the treatment of human pancreatic carcinoma.

(1) The MIA PaCA-2 and PASC-1 human pancreatic cancer xenografts have been established and are useful models for evaluating new antitumor agents; (2) Gemcitabine, adriamycine, and 5-FU were inactive against both MIA PaCA and PASC-2 xenografted tumors, whereas taxol and the diaryl sulfonylureas were active against only one or the other; and (3)
(1) The MIA PaCA-2 and PANT-1 human pancreatic cancer cell lines and their corresponding xenografts were established and used to evaluate new agents against human pancreatic carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel anticancer agents for the treatment of human pancreatic cancer.
the discovery and development of new agents that have activity against human pancreatic carcinoma.
the discovery of new anticancer compounds, and the evaluation of these compounds in human pancreatic carcinoma xenographs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MIA PaCA-2 and PANTC-1 xenografted models were useful to predict antitumor activity of the new anticancer agents tested.
the MIA PaC-2 and PNC-1 xenografted human pancreatic carcinoma models are useful for selecting new potential candidates for therapy for human pancreatic cancer.
gemcitabine, sulofenur, and taxol were active in one of the models, whereas 5-fluouracil and cisplatin were active in neither.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
taxol and the diarylsulfonyls (DSU) are the most promising new agents for pancreatic cancer.
the MIA PaCA-2 xenografted model was more sensitive to the tested drugs, whereas the PANC-1 model was less sensitive to the tested agents.
the PANC-1 model appears to be more sensitive to chemotherapy than the MIA PaC2-2 model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MIA PaC-2 xenograt model is not a good predictor of response to taxol.
the MIA PaCA-2 and PNC-1 xenografted models can be used for screening of potential candidates for therapy for pancreatic cancer.
the MIA PaPaCa2 xenograft model is not a good predictor of activity of taxol and the PANC1 model is not a predictor of activity of DSU.
